A 16-year-old boy presents to an ophthalmologist with blurry vision.
Over the past several months, he has had increasing difficulty seeing the board from the back of the classroom at school.
His medical history is otherwise significant for scoliosis which is managed by an orthopedic surgeon.
His temperature is 98.6°F (37°C), blood pressure is 115/71 mmHg, pulse is 72/min, and respirations are 12/min.
On physical exam, the patient is tall for his age and has long arms.
He has 20 degrees of thoracic scoliosis, which is stable from previous exams.
The patient is otherwise doing well in school and enjoys playing basketball.
